sections: FQR publishes FQG without waiting for the TSO completion ACK

diagram_evidence.render_observation: Rendered inline and opened in GitHub's full-width Mermaid dialog. The five participant lanes remained readable while scrolling. FQR selects TSO delivery, leaves the recipient entry inTransit, commits actual grant and optimistic floor, then sends FQG after the TSO event frame. Under HLA_EVOKED, callback return triggers the delivery ACK; a thrown callback skips the ACK and leaves the recipient inTransit while the later FQG task remains queued until another Evoke. Under HLA_IMMEDIATE, normal callback return ACKs before the continuing event pump submits FQG; a thrown callback unwinds inline, stops extraction before a later FQG event, stores the callback exception, and a later pump dispatches FQG. The optional Resign or ConnectionLost path unregisters the recipient and discards queued and inTransit TSO state. The guide labels the callback-throw interleavings source-derived and not a focused tested interleaving. This is 2025 configured-process profile behavior, not a normative cross-member callback-order rule. The raw Mermaid body hash matches candidate branch source and the local visual ledger.
